Requirement_Summary: License data must live on Address (not Account) so an HCP with several practice states/addresses has a per-address license.
SF_Evidence: No Address object exists in the org at all (`find force-app/main/default/objects -iname "*address*"` returns nothing). License fields (License_Number__c, License_Expiry_Date__c, License_Verification_Status__c, Medical_Council_Reg_Number__c, Controlled_Substance_License__c) live directly on Sciagen_Account__c (force-app/main/default/objects/Sciagen_Account__c/fields/*.field-meta.xml), one value per account regardless of practice locations/states. No Sample_Jurisdiction_Rule__mdt.License_Scope__c exists.
iOS_Evidence: HCP struct (SciagenCRM/Models/Models.swift:126-198) has one flat licenseNumber field and flat address fields (address/city/state/pincode); no Address struct exists anywhere in the iOS codebase (confirmed by exhaustive grep in prior inventory pass).
Risk_Notes: This is the #2 high-risk area flagged for the report. Requires a new Address__c object, migration of the 41 populated License_Number__c account records to per-address rows, and rework of every downstream consumer (SampleEligibilityService, HcpLicenseExpiryBatch, iOS HCP model). Blocks SM-LIC-04 through SM-LIC-20 and SM-CS-01/02.

Requirement_Summary: A License Valid To Sample formula decides, per address, whether the account can receive/sign for samples there.
SF_Evidence: Sciagen_Account__c.Sample_Eligible__c formula (fields/Sample_Eligible__c.field-meta.xml): AND(ISPICKVAL(License_Verification_Status__c,'Verified'), NOT(ISBLANK(License_Expiry_Date__c)), License_Expiry_Date__c>=TODAY(), Can_Prescribe__c). iOS_Evidence: No equivalent computed eligibility indicator is shipped to or computed on the device.

Requirement_Summary: Signature is always required when a drop contains at least one controlled substance, even with a valid Sample Opt-In or non-controlled lines present.
SF_Evidence: SampleDropService.cls:33 sets Needs_Signature__c = p.Requires_Signature__c==true || p.Is_Controlled_Substance__c==true per line; beforeCallUpdate (lines 161-169) blocks submission of the whole call (c.addError(...)) when any line has Needs_Signature__c=true and Signature_Captured__c!=true. This check is independent of, and not overridden by, the opt-in consent logic in SampleEligibilityService.cls:70-74, matching the "even with valid opt-in" requirement.
iOS_Evidence: The CVR's "Capture Signature" action (Views/CLMViews.swift) is a boolean-flag append with no gating logic at all (per iOS inventory section 5.2/6), and the iOS ProductCatalogItem model carries no Is_Controlled_Substance__c/Requires_Signature__c field, so the client cannot even know a line is controlled.
Risk_Notes: iOS could let a rep submit an apparently-complete controlled-substance call with no signature; the server would correctly reject it on sync (matching the spec's fail-safe intent in section 0), but there is no client-side pre-check to prevent the bad late-rejection UX -- a concrete offline/online rule-parity gap (see notes doc).

Requirement_Summary: Layout-level config toggle that marks sections where license/signature checks are skipped (non-PDMA/opt-in contexts), with controlled substances always overriding it.

iOS_Evidence: No equivalent client-side.
Risk_Notes: Lower priority: mostly a US-pack (PDMA) nuance; IN-UCPMP (the default pack) has no "no-signature" exemption path per spec section 16.

Requirement_Summary: IN-UCPMP: products flagged Hypnotic/Sedative/Tranquillizer are hard-blocked from lots, transfers-to-reps, calls, and BRCs (UCPMP 5.1(ii)(f)).
SF_Evidence: Product__c.Is_Restricted__c + Restriction_Reason__c (picklist value Hypnotic_Sedative_Tranquillizer, objects/Product__c/fields/Restriction_Reason__c.field-meta.xml) is hard-blocked at two independent enforcement points: SampleEligibilityService.cls:54-57 (blocks calls/disbursements, cites UCPMP 2024 Clause 5.1(ii)(f)) and SampleTransactionService.cls:143 (blocks all transaction types -- Receipt/Transfer/Return/Adjustment -- "This product is restricted and can not be sampled"). Also logged for audit via SampleAttemptLogService.cls:19 ('hypnotic'->'Restricted_Product') into Sample_Blocked_Attempt__c. Gap: Sample_Lot__c creation itself (SampleLotService.cls) has no restriction check (confirmed by grep -- zero hits), and the BRC channel doesn't exist anywhere in this codebase at all, so the "BRCs" part of the requirement is N/A pending BRC (SM-GEN-02) being built.
iOS_Evidence: No restriction check anywhere client-side; the SampleDrop/ProductCatalogItem models carry no Is_Restricted__c/Restriction_Reason__c field, and the sample-add flow (Views/CLMViews.swift:841-879) has no such gate -- only the unrelated 3-hardcoded-product yearly cap exists.
Risk_Notes: SF-side is one of the most solidly built pieces in this entire scope and should be reused directly once Product Catalog fields are renamed/extended to match spec naming (Therapeutic_Restriction__c) -- but iOS has zero parity, so an offline rep today could stage a hypnotic-product sample line locally with no warning until server rejection on sync.
